## Personality

Mrs. Rachel Lynde is an outspoken and critical woman who prides herself on speaking her mind without fear or favor and judging human nature. Despite her somewhat officious nature, she possesses a kindly and kind-hearted soul, never shirking her share of work. A devoutly pious individual, she holds strict religious and moral views, considering activities such as horse racing and play-acting to be abominations, while taking her duty as a church member seriously. She is also a red-hot, opinionated politician and a farseeing woman who dearly loves to be asked for advice. Highly skilled in domestic pursuits, she enjoys sewing and excels at making homemade butter and cheese.

## History

Mrs. Rachel Lynde, an [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) resident who previously went to school with a red-haired girl, first spots [Matthew Cuthbert](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) driving out of town in unusually fine clothes. Prompted by curiosity, she visits [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) and learns of the Cuthberts' plan to adopt an orphan boy, expressing strong skepticism before leaving to spread the news. Later, during another visit to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), Mrs. Rachel severely insults Anne's looks, inciting a furious outburst from the girl; however, she grants her forgiveness after [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) delivers a dramatic, performed apology. As a close neighbor and friend, she offers [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) practical advice on managing Anne's temper and reports on local mishaps, such as [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) unintentionally serving [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md) currant wine. When [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) decides to surprise [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) with a dress featuring puffed sleeves for Christmas, Mrs. Rachel quietly assists him by purchasing the fabric and sewing the garment in secret. As [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) grows older, Mrs. Rachel visits [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) to praise her maturity and discuss Matthew's failing health with [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md).

## Quotes

> "I just guess she has done well, and far be it from me to be backward in saying it. You’re a credit to your friends, Anne, that’s what, and we’re all proud of you."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v1 CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out P48](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0048)

> "Child, yes, I’m afraid of it. Look at his face. When you’ve seen that look as often as I have you’ll know what it means."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVII. The Reaper Whose Name Is Death P7](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0007)

> "I was kind of afraid you weren’t, though, when I saw Matthew starting off today. I thought maybe he was going to the doctor’s."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P14](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0014)

> "She’s terrible skinny and homely, Marilla. Come here, child, and let me have a look at you. Lawful heart, did any one ever see such freckles? And hair as red as carrots! Come here, child, I say."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v1 CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Properly Horrified P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014)

> "I don’t know it. I guess you’re going to teach right here in Avonlea. The trustees have decided to give you the school."
>
> — Rachel Lynde — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road P36](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0036)

## Relationships

### [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/marilla-cuthbert--rachel-lynde.md)

Mrs. Rachel Lynde is a neighbor and friend to [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md), often visiting [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) to discuss community news and offer outspoken opinions. [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) values Mrs. Rachel's experience and actively seeks her counsel on domestic and child-rearing matters, such as how to handle Anne's stubbornness when she refuses to attend school. Their relationship endures despite occasional friction, such as when [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) reacts furiously to Mrs. Rachel's blunt insults about her appearance, leading Mrs. Rachel to accept a dramatic apology from the girl.

- Friend of — neighborly acquaintance who seeks her advice  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P12](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0012), [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P83](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0083), [v1 CHAPTER XXX. The Queen’s Class Is Organized P40](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0040)</sub>

### [Thomas](../character/thomas.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/rachel-lynde--thomas.md)

[Thomas](../character/thomas.md) Lynde is the husband of Mrs. Rachel Lynde. The two live together in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), where Mrs. Rachel manages the household while keeping a close eye on local affairs. While [Thomas](../character/thomas.md) is mentioned in connection with community events and Mrs. Rachel's social outings, he generally remains in the background while his wife takes the lead in neighborly interactions.
